walkthroughs.body_html:
Buddhism Option — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Buddhism Option brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Buddhism Option.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many Noble Truths are there?

options: Suffering
No fixed self
Impermanence
Enlightenment

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
The Buddha created the universe.

mcqs.q: What does karma mean in Hindu and Buddhist thought?
options: The principle that actions have moral consequences shaping future experience or rebirth — not fate, but ethical cause and effect built into reality.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
Karma is when bad things happen to bad people as punishment.
The Buddha created the universe.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.
